chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Abdullah ibn Ja'far, from Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Sayf al-Tammar, who said:

One of our companions fell ill in Mecca and became delirious/hallucinated, so I visited Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) and informed him. He said to me: 'Give him to drink the suweeq of barley, for it cures, God willing, and it is nourishment in the stomach of the sick.' He said: 'We did not give him the suweeq except for two days' (or he said 'twice') until our companion was healed.

key_terms.الشَّعِير: Barley, specifically referring to barley flour used in the suweeq.
key_terms.بُرْسِمَ: He became delirious or hallucinated, a symptom of fever or illness.
key_terms.سَوِيق: Suweeq, a traditional food made from roasted flour mixed with water, oil, or honey, often used as medicine or light food.
key_terms.غِذَاءٌ: Nourishment/food, highlighting the dual purpose of the remedy.
key_terms.يُعَافِي: It cures/heals, indicating a medicinal property.

ai.seo_question: What is the medicinal benefit of barley suweeq according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) prescribes barley *suweeq* (a thin porridge or soup) for a sick companion who was suffering from fever and hallucinations, highlighting the Prophet's tradition of using simple, digestible foods for recovery. The text emphasizes the dual nature of this remedy as both a therapeutic agent ('it cures') and sustenance ('nourishment in the stomach'), reflecting the Shia emphasis on practical, natural medicine (*tibb*) rooted in the Imams' teachings. The rapid recovery after just two days or servings underscores the efficacy of this specific dietary prescription in Islamic medical tradition.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Abdullah Bin Ja’far, from Muhammad Bin Khalid, from Sayf, from Sayf Al Tammar who said,

‘One of our friends fell sick at Makkah, and hallucinated. So I went over to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> and let him<sup>asws</sup> know. So he<sup>asws</sup> said to me: ‘Make him drink the Al-Suweyq of barley so he would be healthy, Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Willing; and it is a nourishment in the inside of the sick’.
He (the narrator) said, ‘So we did not make him drink Al-Suweyq except for two days only’ (or said ‘twice’) until he our companion was healthy’.
en.sarwar: 14. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from ‘Abd Allah ibn Ja‘far from Muhammad ibn Khalid from Sayf al-Tammar who has said the following:

“One of our friends became ill in Makkah and began to hallucinate. I went to see abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, and informed him (the Imam) about him. He (the Imam) said, ‘Make him drink sawiq of barley; it will cure him by the will of Allah and it is the food for the stomach of patients.’ He (the narrator) has said, ‘We made him drink it for two days or he said, ‘twice’ our friend was cured.’”
